model_interpretation.claim: Unrolling the inner loop by two on T2 may reduce loop-control overhead while retaining its SWAR popcount. Each update still consumes the result of the preceding update, so the recurrence remains strictly ordered; this dependency may limit any gain. The controller must measure the combined program rather than infer an additive speedup.

model_interpretation.claim: The selected parent uses subtraction to form two-bit population counts. Replacing only that first SWAR stage with masked addition tests whether add-based field aggregation performs better under the frozen compiler; the extra mask/add work may instead make it slower. The remaining count stages and serial recurrence are unchanged. This is distinct from the measured multiply-reduction and nibble-subtraction variants, whose results show that SWAR formulations need measurement rather than presumed ranking.
